The PKGBUILD is safe to run with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. These commands source the PKGBUILD's top-level scope and execute `pkgver()` if present, but in this file, there is no `pkgver()` function. The `pkgver` is statically defined as `0.3.14`, and no command substitution or external execution is used in its assignment.

The `source` array uses a standard HTTPS download from the project's own GitHub repository (`https://github.com/akitaonrails/frank_go`), which is expected and safe. The archive is fetched via a tagged release URL (`v$pkgver.tar.gz`), and while checksums are provided (sha256sums), even if they were 'SKIP', that would not make this stage unsafe — verification happens later, and extraction under `--nobuild` does not execute any code.

There are no top-level command substitutions, network requests outside the declared source, or use of `eval`, `curl | bash`, or other dangerous patterns in the global scope. The `build()` and `package()` functions contain legitimate packaging logic using `npm` and standard file operations, but they are not executed during this phase due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD poses no risk of remote code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
